hook: Over 50 long-lost letters from Mary Stuart were hidden in plain sight.

sections.voiceover: Over 50 long-lost letters from Mary Stuart were hidden in plain sight.
sections.visual_cue: Close up of an aged, handwritten document with complex cipher symbols.
sections.sfx_cue: Soft quill scratching on parchment followed by a subtle digital glitch sound.
b_roll: Historical manuscript page with encrypted symbols

sections.voiceover: In 2021, Satoshi Tomokiyo discovered these encrypted documents inside the Bibliothèque nationale de France. How did Tomokiyo and his international research team finally crack these complex encrypted documents?
sections.visual_cue: Interior shot of the Bibliothèque nationale de France archives showing catalog shelves.
b_roll: Close up of archive catalog labels

text_overlay.text: Found at the Bibliothèque nationale de France

sections.voiceover: But the team had to transcribe 150,000 symbols to make the cipher readable for computers.
sections.visual_cue: Close up of a researcher digitizing symbols into a modern computer interface.
sections.sfx_cue: Fast typing sound transitioning into a digital processing hum.

sections.voiceover: These documents were stored under catalog numbers Français 2988 and Français 20506 for centuries.
sections.visual_cue: Animated overlay of a hill-climbing algorithm processing the cipher text.
sections.sfx_cue: Rising digital chime as the text becomes readable.
b_roll: Portraits of George Lasry, Norbert Biermann, and Satoshi Tomokiyo

sections.voiceover: These 50 letters offer a new view of Mary Stuart.
sections.visual_cue: The original encrypted document slowly fading to reveal transcribed text.
sections.sfx_cue: Final echo of a quill scratch.
b_roll: Close up of the decrypted manuscript page

text_overlay.text: A new view of Mary Stuart
